title: The Influence of a Hole
subtitle: Strong knight outposts justify a material investment

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter VI, §33 The Influence of a Hole, Example 67

narration.say: Janowski has White against Kupchick at Havana in 1913. The opening is a Queen’s Gambit Declined.
Black exchanges on c4, then moves the knight to b6. Capablanca criticises this knight placement.
White retreats the bishop. Black brings the other knight to d5, and the bishops are exchanged.
Both sides castle. White occupies the c-file, and Black plays c6, restricting the bishop on d7.

steps.title: A pawn advance creates an outpost

narration.say: White brings the knight to e4. Black advances f5, creating a hole on e5.
The first knight goes to c5. Black retreats the bishop to e8.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Occupy the hole on e5 with the f3-knight.

narration.say: White centralises the rook and queen. Black lifts the rook toward the kingside.
White secures the position before opening the centre.
White challenges the centre with e4. Black pushes f4, and the queen retreats to f2.
Black’s knight has entered e3. White can exchange a rook for the knight and then recover the capturing pawn.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Sacrifice the rook for the knight on e3.

steps.title: Recover the pawn and improve the pieces

narration.say: White recaptures with the queen. Black retreats the remaining knight to c8.
The e5-knight goes to g4. Black’s rook retreats, and White advances e5.
The bishop joins from c4. Black moves the bishop to f7.

steps.title: A knight deep in the position

narration.say: White can put the knight on f6, supported by the e5-pawn.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Establish the knight on f6.

narration.say: The knight on c5 centralises to e4. Black plays h6.
White advances h4. Black moves the knight to d5, and the queen comes to d2.
White takes on g5. Black brings the queen to f8.
White advances f4 and g4. The final exchange leaves White’s attacking formation intact.
Black resigns. White’s knights dominate the position, and the pawns support the attack.

steps.title: A hole matters when you can occupy it

narration.say: Black’s f-pawn advance created e5 as a lasting knight outpost. White also established a strong knight on c5.
White invested material to preserve the positional advantages and keep the attack coordinated.
A weak square is not just an empty square. It becomes important when a supported piece can occupy it and influence the whole position.
